content:
Harish Reddy: Heads up: for the failover automation work, we need a real answer on fleet readiness if we swing traffic cross-region. Specifically: what headroom do we have per region for Hosted vs Dedicated, and what procurement lead time if we need to add a buffer. This is blocking the “safe-to-failover” checks definition.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. Fleet view right now (rough, from this morning). Biggest constraint is not “total GPUs” but *free headroom in the right pools* + ramp time.

Vanessa Ortiz: Quick numbers (A100/H100 mixed, normalized to “GPU slots”):
```text
Region      Hosted headroom   Dedicated spare   Notes
us-east     ~18%              ~6%               bursty evenings
us-west     ~11%              ~4%               tight on H100
eu-central  ~9%               ~3%               worst-case if US fails over into EU
```
This is assuming current commitments and last 7d p95 utilization.

Miles Thornton: For progressive failover, we’re thinking 5% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% in stages, but only if target has capacity *and* we’re not already in a local incident. Can you translate those headroom % into “max failoverable traffic” safely?

Vanessa Ortiz: Not cleanly, because traffic mix matters (context length + streaming + model mix). But if we simplify: 10% headroom ~= 8–12% traffic depending on batching efficiency. Dedicated is harder bc of pinned capacity.

Harish Reddy: For the “safe-to-failover” gate, can we define something like: target region must have >= X% headroom *and* queue depth below Y for Z minutes?

Vanessa Ortiz: Yes, but we should include a hard guard: no failover into a region that is already above e.g. 85% sustained utilization on the relevant pool. We keep getting burned by “it looks fine” averages.

Irene Choi: Agree. We should be explicit that “headroom” is pool-specific (hosted-general vs hosted-lowlatency vs dedicated-reserved). Also remember cross-region shift can create hot spots in *inference router* and *KV cache mem* before GPU itself saturates.

Mina Haddad: From routing side: we can scope initial prod test to a low-risk slice (one model route + free tier / internal). But eventually the worst case is: us-west impaired and us-east absorbs.

Emily Zhao: Infra note: cross-region failover also hits network. Egress + inter-region RTT changes can increase streaming disconnects if timeouts are too tight. If we move large volumes from EU -> US, we’ll see latency inflation and different TCP loss characteristics.

Victor Alvarez: +1 on network. We need to check:
- edge -> region path health
- region -> dependency paths (auth, policy store)
- interconnect capacity
If we assume “full regional failover,” we should pre-provision bandwidth headroom.

Harish Reddy: Do we have any known bottlenecks on interconnect today?

Victor Alvarez: We’re okay day-to-day, but we don’t currently reserve enough extra for “sudden 50% traffic swing.” We can do it, but it’s not immediate. Some parts are config-only, others are provider quota / circuit changes.

Rafael Mendes: For the project plan: the goal is “degraded but available” first, so even when we fail over we might shed load for lower tiers. But the safe-to-failover checks need a real capacity signal.

Vanessa Ortiz: Procurement lead time:
- If we need *more H100* in us-west: 6–10 weeks depending on supplier allocation.
- A100 is easier: 3–6 weeks.
- If it’s just shifting capacity between pools within a region: days (but can break SLOs for existing tenants).
Also, data center rack/power constraints in eu-central are real. We can’t just “add 20%” quickly there.

Irene Choi: So for automation: we should assume we can’t buy our way out quickly. The design must be robust with current buffers + progressive failover + load shedding.

Miles Thornton: Makes sense. But for the go/no-go of the prod controlled test, we should agree on minimum headroom requirement. Suggest:
- Target region >= 15% headroom in hosted-general pool
- Target region queue depth p95 < threshold for 10m
- No active “capacity incident” in target
- Dependency health green (auth/policy store)

Harish Reddy: 15% seems high given today’s numbers.

Vanessa Ortiz: Yeah, 15% in eu-central is not happening without reallocations. For US->US tests, maybe. For EU, we’d need to keep the blast radius tiny.

Mina Haddad: That’s okay. First controlled failover doesn’t need to be EU or full-route. We can do us-east <-> us-west for a single model route. We just need a clean matrix of what’s feasible.

Emily Zhao: Also note: shifting us-west -> us-east increases latency for west coast clients unless edge routing also shifts. If we only change backend region without edge steering, clients may still hit their nearest POP and then hairpin. That can be OK but we should measure.

Victor Alvarez: On DNS TTL / edge steering: we can keep TTL conservative for game day (like 60s) but in real incidents caches vary. We shouldn’t assume “instant” traffic movement.

Connor O'Brien: From release/change mgmt: we need a documented capacity “pre-flight checklist” before enabling the feature flag in prod. If headroom is marginal, we block.

Harish Reddy: Can someone own the pre-flight doc and the canonical signals? I want something the trigger engine can query (or at least that SRE can quickly validate).

Vanessa Ortiz: I can draft a minimal set:
- `gpu_pool_utilization{region,pool}` (p95 + sustained)
- `gpu_pool_headroom_slots{region,pool}`
- `inference_queue_depth{region,route}` (p95)
- `autoscaler_pending_nodes{region,pool}`
- `capacity_incident_flag{region}` (manual)
And then a human-readable “OK/NOT OK” summary.

Irene Choi: Good. Let’s also include “time to add headroom” notes so on-call doesn’t go chasing impossible asks mid-incident.

Rafael Mendes: Action items:
1) Vanessa: draft pre-flight checklist + thresholds proposal (by EOW)
2) Victor/Emily: note network constraints + any provider lead times (also EOW)
3) Harish: summarize procurement lead times in the project notes + propose buffer strategy for Q2

Harish Reddy: Works. One more Q: what buffer do we actually want long-term? If we want automated failover to be safe, we probably need a standing N+?%

Vanessa Ortiz: For Hosted, I’d argue we need ~20% *effective* headroom in at least one paired region (or the ability to shed ~10–15% traffic on failover). For Dedicated, we need contractual language / explicit “failover capacity” add-on; otherwise we’re pretending.

Mina Haddad: +1. Routing can do tier-based protections, but we need to be honest about what happens for dedicated tenants.

Irene Choi: Let’s capture that in the doc: automation only guarantees “attempt” unless dedicated failover capacity is pre-reserved.

Connor O'Brien: Please add a line about this to the go/no-go template. We’ll get asked during approval.

Harish Reddy: Cool. I’ll update the capacity section in the failover notes once Vanessa drops the checklist. Thanks all.
